x: B is incorrect: the Constitution originally had 10 Fundamental Duties (added by the 42nd Amendment, 1976, on the Swaran Singh Committee's advice); the 11th was added by the 86th Amendment in 2002.
t: Remember 10 duties first, the 11th in 2002.

x: Both are true and R explains A: Fundamental Duties are non-justiciable precisely because courts cannot enforce them directly and there is no legal penalty for breaking them.
t: Check whether R defines 'non-justiciable'.

x: Both are true: Fundamental Rights are justiciable claims against the State, while Fundamental Duties are non-justiciable moral obligations on citizens.
t: Contrast rights against the State with duties of citizens.

x: Part IVA – contains the duties; Article 51A – lists them; 42nd Amendment, 1976 – added them; Swaran Singh Committee – recommended them.
t: Match Part, Article, amendment and committee.

x: Three: Fundamental Duties are non-justiciable, apply only to citizens and are moral obligations. 'Available against the State' describes Fundamental Rights.
t: Spot the feature that belongs to Fundamental Rights.

x: Duty (a) of Article 51A: abide by the Constitution and respect its ideals and institutions, the National Flag and the National Anthem — each item matches its own object.
t: Match each verb to its object.

x: All four are correct: citizens must cherish the ideals of the freedom struggle and uphold and protect the sovereignty, unity and integrity of India (Article 51A(b) and (c)).
t: Recall duties (b) and (c).

x: Defend the country – the defence duty; render national service – when called upon; promote harmony – among all the people of India; common brotherhood – the brotherhood duty (Article 51A(d) and (e)).
t: Match each phrase to the part of the duty it completes.

x: Both are true and R explains A: because the duty is to promote harmony among all the people of India, it must cut across religious, linguistic, regional and sectional differences.
t: Ask whether 'all the people' explains 'transcending diversities'.

x: Article 51A(e) requires citizens to renounce practices derogatory to the dignity of women. The other options reverse real duties.
t: Look for the option that is not a reversed duty.

x: Both are true: citizens must value and preserve India's composite culture (51A(f)) and protect and improve the natural environment (51A(g)).
t: Recall duties (f) and (g).

x: I, II and III are correct: the duty is to protect and improve the natural environment, including forests, lakes, rivers and wildlife, and to have compassion for living creatures. IV wrongly limits it to forests and rivers.
t: Watch for 'only' narrowing a duty.

x: Article 51A(h): develop scientific temper (scientific outlook), humanism (concern for humanity) and the spirit of inquiry (questioning) and reform (improvement).
t: Match each quality to its meaning.

x: Citizens must safeguard public property and abjure violence (51A(i)), and strive for excellence in every sphere of individual and collective activity (51A(j)).
t: Pair each verb with its object.

x: Both are true and R explains A: striving for excellence in both individual and collective activity is what lets the nation rise to higher levels of endeavour and achievement.
t: Ask whether R is the means to the goal in A.

x: Article 51A(k) asks a parent or guardian to provide educational opportunities to his or her child or ward aged 6 to 14. It is not a duty towards all children.
t: Note the duty is towards one's own child or ward.

x: Both are true: the 11th duty, Article 51A(k), concerns educational opportunities for a child or ward between six and fourteen years.
t: Recall the age range 6–14.

x: All three are correct: Parliament can enforce duties by law, and courts use them to interpret unclear laws and to judge whether a law is reasonable and constitutional.
t: Recall how non-justiciable duties still matter.

x: The Fundamental Duties were inspired by the Constitution of the former USSR. The USA gave Fundamental Rights, France the ideals of liberty, equality and fraternity, and the UK parliamentary government.
t: Link duties to the USSR.

x: C is incorrect: the 42nd Amendment came into force on 3 January 1977, not 4 January. Duties are in Part IVA, Article 51A.
t: Check the exact date.

x: Both are true and R explains A: the 11th duty is clause (k) of Article 51A, which concerns education for children aged 6–14.
t: Ask whether R names the clause behind A.

x: Clause (e) – harmony and dignity of women; (f) – composite culture; (g) – natural environment; (h) – scientific temper, humanism and inquiry.
t: Recall the order of clauses (e) to (h).

x: All three are correct: the Fundamental Duties were added in 1976 by the 42nd Amendment on the Swaran Singh Committee's recommendation.
t: Recall the year, amendment and committee.

x: Clause (a) – abide by the Constitution and respect the Flag and Anthem; (b) – cherish the ideals of the freedom struggle; (c) – uphold sovereignty, unity and integrity; (d) – defend the country.
t: Recall the order of the first four duties.

x: Two: Article 51A(i) asks citizens to safeguard public property and abjure violence. Striving towards excellence is clause (j).
t: Separate clause (i) from clause (j).

x: Both are true and R explains A: Part IVA has only one Article, which is Article 51A listing all 11 duties.
t: Check whether R names the one Article in A.
